member.name: T:Microsoft.Testing.Platform.IPC.NamedPipeServerSecurity
member.summary: Windows-only helpers that create a controller named pipe whose discretionary access control list (DACL) keeps the current-user protection of PipeOptions.CurrentUserOnly while additionally authorizing a small, explicitly requested set of AppContainer package SIDs.

remarks.para: Why this exists. On Windows, .NET implements PipeOptions.CurrentUserOnly with a security descriptor whose owner is the creating token's owner SID and whose DACL contains a single ACE granting that same SID full control. An AppContainer (UWP, or a WinUI app configured for AppContainer) runs with a restricted token: Windows performs the normal access check against the token's user/group SIDs and a second check against the token's restricting SIDs, which for an AppContainer contain the package SID. Access is granted only when both checks succeed, so a DACL that names only the user SID denies the AppContainer client even though it belongs to the same signed-in user. Knowing the pipe name is therefore not enough — the package SID must appear in the DACL. See https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/secauthz/restricted-tokens.
Security model. The descriptor produced here is deliberately minimal and fully explicit:

list.item: Owner and group are the current token's owner SID, exactly like PipeOptions.CurrentUserOnly. This preserves the elevation split (an elevated token's owner is BUILTIN\Administrators, a non-elevated one's is the user) and keeps the client-side PipeOptions.CurrentUserOnly owner validation working.
The DACL is protected (P), so no inherited ACE can widen it.
The owner SID gets FILE_ALL_ACCESS-equivalent rights (the same mask .NET grants).

Every authorized package SID gets only — read, write, read the security descriptor (needed by the client-side owner validation) and synchronize. Notably it does not include FILE_CREATE_PIPE_INSTANCE, so an authorized package can never create another instance of the pipe and impersonate the controller.

Only genuine AppContainer SIDs may be authorized (see ). The catch-all ALL APPLICATION PACKAGES / ALL RESTRICTED APPLICATION PACKAGES SIDs, user SIDs, group SIDs and Everyone are rejected by construction, so the extension point that feeds this type can only ever widen access to one specific packaged application.
The pipe additionally rejects remote clients (PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS), which the default .NET pipe does not do.

No mandatory integrity label is emitted, so the pipe keeps the controller's own integrity level and Mandatory Integrity Control remains a second gate behind the DACL. An AppContainer client is admitted by its package-SID ACE alone.

remarks.para: The implementation goes through CreateNamedPipeW rather than PipeSecurity because the managed ACL types are not part of the netstandard2.0 surface this assembly also builds for, and because PipeOptions.CurrentUserOnly cannot be combined with an explicit descriptor.

member.name: M:Microsoft.Testing.Platform.OutputDevice.TargetFrameworkParser.GetShortTargetFrameworkIncludingPlatform(System.Reflection.Assembly)
member.summary: Resolves the short target framework moniker of , including the platform component (e.g. net8.0-windows10.0.18362.0) when the assembly was built for a platform-specific TFM, including non-OS / custom platform identifiers such as Uno's browserwasm.
member.remarks: A plain net8.0 build and a net8.0-windows10.0.18362.0 build carry the exact same (.NETCoreApp,Version=v8.0) and produce the same , so the short TFM alone cannot tell them apart. The only runtime-visible signal is System.Runtime.Versioning.TargetPlatformAttribute, which the SDK emits for any platform-specific TFM (including non-OS / custom platform identifiers such as Uno's browserwasm). Appending it here keeps report file names unique per build so two modules of the same assembly no longer overwrite each other's report.

member.name: T:System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.DynamicallyAccessedMembersAttribute
member.summary: Indicates that certain members on a specified are accessed dynamically, for example through .
member.remarks:
This allows tools to understand which members are being accessed during the execution of a program.
This attribute is valid on members whose type is or .
When this attribute is applied to a location of type , the assumption is that the string represents a fully qualified type name.
When this attribute is applied to a class, interface, or struct, the members specified can be accessed dynamically on instances returned from calling on instances of that class, interface, or struct.
If the attribute is applied to a method it's treated as a special case and it implies the attribute should be applied to the "this" parameter of the method. As such the attribute should only be used on instance methods of types assignable to System.Type (or string, but no methods will use it there).
